### [1/10] HEADER — Tickets-repo unbounded growth: reconciler .bridge_state deep-dive (TABLED)

PROBLEM: The rebar tickets git store (.tickets-tracker, `tickets` branch) grows UNBOUNDEDLY. ~443 MB / ~178k objects for ~15k tickets; ~85% is the reconciler's `.bridge_state/` Jira-sync cache. Goal: bound the growth without breaking the reconciler, cross-clone union-merge sync, or the identity/attestation trust model.

STATUS: **TABLED.** This is a sensitive reconciler-CORE change (touches direction arbitration + the differ field contract). We deep-dived the WHY of the current design (Chesterton's fence) and are deferring implementation. THIS session_log = the comprehensive raw record; IDEA <linked below> = the summary + resume pointer.

RESUME MAP:
- Prior session log b96a-15a5-1c0a-47c5 (closein-vermillion-azurevase): earlier measured facts + the cited growth prior-art research report (git-annex forget / crates.io / Homebrew).
- Umbrella: ticket 1270-b740 (Jira reconciler deep-dive). Convergence history: epics 3006-e198 (Level-triggered bridge convergence), 6c9c-811f (dust-troth-naval / conflict-free reconciler state), 97e7-cf42 (minor-haste-ogle / union+gc). ADRs 0004, 0026-0029, 0031.
- ACTIVE OTHER SESSION: epic 58b0-104b (Jira reconciler: silent comment + inbound-link SYNC-CORRECTNESS) — orthogonal to SIZE, but shares the differ/field contract, so COORDINATE on any snapshot/baseline change.
- OUT OF SCOPE: gc-corruption fix (bug 88eb, "ADR 0051", Gerrit 774 — LANDED); verify-identity scan cost (another session).

ENTRIES BELOW: [2] measured facts; [3] prev_snapshot NOT redundant (correction); [4] prev narrowing lever + THE OPEN GATE; [5] bindings.json growth + levers; [6] DOSSIER A snapshot substrate WHY; [7] DOSSIER B baseline lineage WHY + digest risk; [8] DOSSIER C binding lifecycle/identity WHY; [9] DOSSIER D coordination/storage WHY + reclaim flag-day; [10] decisions + recommended plan + open gates.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [2/10] MEASURED FACTS (repo size breakdown; do not re-derive)

- Repo ~443 MB / ~178k objects for ~15k tickets. PACKED SIZE: blobs 424 MB (95.7%), trees 10.7 MB (2.4%), commits 8.2 MB (1.8%). => tree churn / directory sharding / active-vs-archive split are the WRONG levers for SIZE (git deltas trees to ~0; sharding was measured to INCREASE object count 2.00->3.00 trees/commit). Do NOT reopen those.
- `.bridge_state/` = ~375 MB (~85%): bindings.json 219 MB / ~987 committed versions; prev_snapshot.json 155 MB / ~4450 versions; bindings-retired.json ~886 B.
- Actual ticket/event blobs ~35 MB, slow growth.
- CURRENT WORKTREE sizes (measured this session): bindings.json 13.9-14.6 MB across 1235 CONFIRMED bindings (only the bound subset of ~15k tickets); prev_snapshot.json 24.1 MB across ~2050 fetched Jira issues; bindings-retired.json 886 B.
- Serialization is ALREADY canonical for both files: json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True), dict-keyed (bindings by local_id; prev by jira_key). Reformatting buys NOTHING; the growth is genuine content churn + over-provisioned payloads (see [4],[5]).
- Nothing reads the git HISTORY of any .bridge_state file — every consumer (reconciler, fsck, identity/authorship trust scan) reads only the CURRENT worktree copy. So bridge_state history's ONLY value is human debugging.

CONSTRAINTS: readers use the WORKTREE not history; cross-clone sync = union-merge of the tickets branch (`.bridge_state/* merge=ours`, local-wins, reconciler rebuilds loser); single-writer via refs/reconciler/lock; the reconciler runs on EPHEMERAL GitHub-Actions runners (*/20 cron) so state must be committed to survive; every write auto-commits+auto-pushes to origin/tickets.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [3/10] KEY FINDING — prev_snapshot.json is NOT redundant (CORRECTION of an earlier framing)

An earlier hypothesis "prev_snapshot is redundant, delete it" was PROVEN WRONG by two independent adversarial subagents (red-team hunt-the-breaker + blue-team prove-removable) that CONVERGED, plus direct code reads. DO NOT DELETE prev_snapshot.

WHAT IS TRUE:
- prev_snapshot's DIRECTION-ARBITRATION role IS fully replaced by the per-binding baseline in bindings.json. Proven EMPIRICALLY (not just reasoning): rollout ticket a118-fa8e recorded 30 consecutive divergent=0 shadow passes over ~4h across ~854 bindings + a byte-identical flip pass; d6bd-95c9 hardcoded baseline-consumer-swap always-on; direction test tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_arbitration.py::test_dryrun_arbitration_pinned_to_baseline feeds a STALE prev_snapshot and asserts the baseline wins. outbound_differ.py:795 -> outbound_fields.py:416-418 overrides arbitration_prev = get_baseline(local_id); the prev_snapshot arg there is a FIXTURE-ONLY fallback = DEAD in prod.
- BUT arbitration is only 1 of ~6 consumers. prev_snapshot is STILL LOAD-BEARING as the EDGE-TRIGGER ANCESTOR: run_differs.py:198 calls differ.compute_mutations(prev_snapshot, curr_snapshot) UNCONDITIONALLY every pass; differ.py:299 "key in jira_state only -> inbound create". Empty prev => every Jira key looks new => re-emits the documented "2050+ inbound_create mutations on every pass" regression (reconcile.py:662-669). The baseline CANNOT cover this — it is keyed by local_id, CONFIRMED-bindings only, with NO representation of UNBOUND native Jira issues.
- Other live prev consumers with no baseline equivalent: dual-identity invariant check_dual_identity_complete (run_differs.py:265, invariants.py:234+) — currently INERT because the fetcher never writes local_id into snapshot entries (differ.py:457-459); edge/level adoption coordination (binding_walk.py:200-218 skip_adopt_keys); corrupt-merge safety canary (_handle_corrupt_snapshot reconcile.py:715-768, also a tickets-branch-partial-merge tripwire); bridge_fsck drift oracle.
- STALE BELIEF corrected: d6bd's keep-reason "needed to advance/seed baselines" is stale — _advance_baselines reads curr not prev (reconcile.py:928); seed_baselines_from_snapshot has ZERO src/ callers (dead code). The REAL reason prev stays alive is the edge-trigger, which d6bd never enumerated.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [4/10] LEVER — narrow prev_snapshot to a KEY-SET + THE ONE OPEN GATE that blocks it

prev_snapshot is NOT redundant but is GROSSLY OVER-PROVISIONED. It stores the full ACLI field payload per issue (fetcher.py:413 + parent/comment/issuelinks enrichments, ~12 KB/issue, volatile fields updated/created/watches/worklog tick every pass) — but its live consumers need at MOST the SET of jira_keys seen last pass. Sizing trace (differ branches):
- Branch (1) inbound-create `_compute_mutations_emit_jira_only` reads prev ONLY via key-membership (`in_local = key in local_state`); zero field reads. THE sole non-deletable role.
- Branch (3) field-drift `_compute_mutations_emit_both`: reads full fields BUT its emitted (outbound,update) values are DROPPED at _mutation_to_batch_dict (batch_dispatch.py:107-110 looks for `changed_fields`; branch-3 writes a bare dict -> {} -> empty no-op update_issue). => prev does NOT need the 5 mirrored fields for drift.
- dual-identity invariant: inert (fetcher never writes local_id). rebar-id/phantom-guard: reads CURR labels not prev. seed_baselines: dead.
- So prev can shrink to a bare KEY-SET: 24 MB -> ~25 KB current, and version count 4450 -> ~membership-changes (volatile churn gone). Near-eliminates prev as a growth driver. NO delete, NO history rewrite, NO new ref.

SHAPE CONSTRAINT (dossier A): store the narrowed prev as a DICT `{jira_key: {}}`, NOT a literal `set` — check_dual_identity_complete and _emit_both's `local_state[key] or {}` guards assume dict entries.

*** THE ONE OPEN GATE — resolve BEFORE implementing (two subagents partially disagree): ***
Narrowing to a key-set is NOT equivalent to prev={}. With prev={} (no keys) every curr key routes to _emit_jira_only and _emit_both NEVER runs ("expensive but safe", reconcile.py:727). With a key-set {key:{}}, _emit_both RE-ACTIVATES with a NULL ancestor: for keys in BOTH prev and curr, resolve_state(None, curr_val) returns local_val=None (conflict_resolver.py:28-49) -> changed[field]=None -> an outbound update that CLEARS status/assignee/priority/title for every key present in both, EVERY pass = DATA LOSS, *IF _emit_both is authoritative*.
- Sizing agent claim: branch-3 output is DROPPED at _mutation_to_batch_dict (no changed_fields key) -> harmless empty no-op. => narrowing safe.
- Dossier A: did NOT confirm that batch-conversion trace; flags _emit_both (differ.py:556-607, fed run_differs.py:198-200) as THE fence. resolve_state returns the prev value for FIELD_CLASSES status/assignee/priority/title/type.
RESOLUTION REQUIRED (pick one, verified by a corpus mutation-diff prev-full vs prev-keyset): (i) PROVE _emit_both outbound updates are superseded/dropped by the binding-aware compute_outbound_mutations (run_differs.py:456-467) — differ.py:7-11 calls the (prev,next) form "the LEGACY snapshot-diff contract it replaces"; OR (ii) make the snapshot-differ skip the both-path for empty-value prev entries (route to create/adopt); OR (iii) stop feeding prev as local_state to compute_mutations entirely.
ALSO verify: branch-(2) neutering (outbound-CREATE for keys in prev-not-curr; branch-2 payload DOES reach Jira) — narrowing makes it emit nothing; this is very likely a CORRECTNESS IMPROVEMENT aligning with ADR 0028 (absence != deletion; the level-triggered binding-walk already covers bound-but-absent via direct GET), but confirm via the same corpus diff.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [5/10] bindings.json GROWTH + LEVERS (measured on the live 14.6 MB file, 1235 bindings)

CONTENT BREAKDOWN: baseline = 96.8% of each entry; within baseline, description = 86.1% (stored as the full Jira ADF dict, NOT plain text — mean 5787 B, median 4088 B, max 31,850 B; 6.81 MB total across 1235). status/priority are full Jira objects too. Identity (local_id/jira_key) + bookkeeping ~3%.

DOMINANT GROWTH DRIVER = `baseline_advanced_at`, a WRITE-ONLY timestamp bumped UNCONDITIONALLY on ~all in-window bindings every pass. set_baseline (binding_store.py:371-375) rewrites baseline + stamps baseline_advanced_at = now() with NO "did the value change?" guard; _advance_baselines (reconcile.py:914-930, called :965) loops ALL confirmed in-window bindings every persist pass. PROOF: 1134/1235 entries (92%) share ONE baseline_advanced_at second from the last pass. baseline_advanced_at is NEVER READ anywhere. => bindings.json changes on essentially EVERY pass, editing a scattered timestamp across 92% of a sort-ordered file = pathological for git delta. ~987 versions ~= ~987 passes (NOT "passes where a value changed"), deltas ~222 KB/version.

LEVERS (safest-first, measured whole-file sizes):
1. CHURN GUARD (biggest bang, provably safe, no equality change): drop `baseline_advanced_at` (or bump only on real change) + add a write-when-changed guard in set_baseline so a no-op advance leaves the entry (and the file blob) byte-identical -> git dedups -> ZERO new version. This attacks the VERSION COUNT (the 987), not just per-version size. Without it, a content lever alone still emits ~1 version/pass forever (reclaimed 219 MB returns in ~2 months).
2. TEXT NORMALIZE (-66%: 14.64 MB -> 4.97 MB, near-zero risk, NO migration): store description as adf_to_text(...) and status/priority as `.name` inside set_baseline. Behavior-preserving BY CONSTRUCTION — it stores exactly the projection the comparison already computes via _extract_jira_field (outbound_fields.py:201-234); _extract_jira_field already passes a plain-string baseline straight through, and reads both ADF-dict and text forms, so old+new entries coexist and auto-convert within ~1 pass. Leave `assignee` un-normalized (3.2%, usually null; its dict enables _assignee_matches multi-form tolerance).
3. DIGEST (sha256 of normalized value, -92%: -> 1.14 MB) — OPTIONAL, higher risk (equality-kernel change + migration + one-way value). NOT needed for sustainability; (1)+(2) already make growth sustainable. If pursued, gate exactly like the prev->baseline rollout (dual-write shadow -> N divergent=0 passes -> flag flip -> retire). See [7] for the assignee KILLER.

OTHER: reverse index is derivable but only 0.3% of the file and read directly by _ids.py:67 in ordinary clones -> not worth changing. Retired entries already compacted OUT (popped to separate bindings-retired.json with NO baseline, binding_store.py:428-439) -> do not bloat bindings.json.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [6/10] DOSSIER A — Snapshot substrate: WHY the reconciler is snapshot-based

DISAMBIGUATION (load-bearing): "snapshot" names THREE unrelated subsystems. (A) Jira reconciler snapshots prev/curr — governed by ADR 0004 only. (B) code-reading gate cache (ADR 0005) = content-addressed git-tree cache for LLM gates — UNRELATED. (C) event-store compaction SNAPSHOT events + replay horizon (ADR 0035) — UNRELATED (the reconciler has NO replay/fold-horizon; it diffs prev-vs-curr). => "prev == a past curr for replay/horizon-safety" is a false import; ADR 0035/0005 do NOT constrain narrowing prev.

WHY SNAPSHOTS AT ALL (not live-per-decision, not a diff log): the ACLI/JQL ceiling — fetcher hits a hard 1000->1200-issue per-query cap with SilentTruncationError (fetcher.py:84-106, _ACLI_CEILING=1200); ~1050 active + ~1120 Done on DIG. Live-per-decision = thousands of round-trips/pass. A diff log can't answer "is this key still present?" which the edge-trigger + census + level-triggered adoption all require (full membership). Snapshot is idempotent/testable (byte-identical on identical data).

WHY prev IS COMMITTED (durable), not in-memory/local: GHA runners are EPHEMERAL — fresh FS every run. Earlier code wrote prev to the main-branch worktree (dies with the run) so prev was always {} and the differ re-derived ALL 2050+ inbound_create mutations every pass (reconcile.py:662-669 verbatim). Fix: write prev under .tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/ so the commit-back step rides it on the tickets branch across runs (reconcile.py:670-673; reconcile-bridge.yml:270-276). Corollary I-FAILCLOSED: a corrupt/conflict-marked prev ABORTS the pass (reconcile.py:678-680, :725-734) because a conflict marker means the tickets branch may be partially merged so curr is also untrustworthy.

PRODUCER<->CONSUMER CONTRACT (ADR 0004, keystone story 8937-eed3, epic f89d): forced by THREE prod bugs of one CLASS where each half was unit-tested against snapshot dicts the real fetcher never emits — 0ee6 (inbound read flat `comments` while fetcher wrote nested `comment`), 3f04 (snapshot never carried `issuelinks` -> link sync structurally dead). Fix: _snapshot_schema.py SSOT (SnapshotEntry TypedDict + JSON Schema) + a STRUCTURE/semantic round-trip test through the production deserialization path (never values/call-counts). SCOPE (critical): validate_snapshot_entry runs ONLY in the contract test, governs the PRODUCER output = CURR, and is NEVER run against prev. So narrowing prev does not violate ADR 0004.

WHY the fetcher stores the FULL payload (not a projection): schema leaves additionalProperties OPEN ("a real issue carries many fields the reconciler doesn't read") — a projection would need widening every time a differ reads a new field, re-opening the 3f04 silently-absent-field failure. Enrichment merges (comment/issuelinks) amortize per-ticket ACLI into one paged REST sweep.

INVARIANTS: I-SCHEMA/I-ROUNDTRIP (curr only); I-DURABLE (prev survives ephemeral runs); I-FAILCLOSED (unparseable prev aborts); I-ANCESTOR (ADR 0026: MUST retain a 3-way-merge baseline for the 5 inbound-mirrored fields; "removing prev_snapshot WITHOUT a replacement last-synced store re-opens 16870dbec and is explicitly rejected"; per-binding baseline is the authorized replacement but "binding-presence is NOT a substitute for the baseline VALUE").

BEARING: narrowing prev to a key-set does NOT violate ADR 0004 (governs curr) nor 0005/0035 (other subsystems). The binding-store baseline already satisfies I-ANCESTOR for the primary consumer. The ONE un-cleared fence = differ._compute_mutations_emit_both (see [4]). Debug artifact (b): keep OUT of the .tickets-tracker commit-back path unless intended on the tickets branch; must NOT be fail-closed (a corrupt debug snapshot must never abort a pass).
Refs: ADR 0004, 0026; reconcile.py:662-768; fetcher.py:84-106,413-527; _snapshot_schema.py; differ.py:263-607; conflict_resolver.py:28-49; run_differs.py:190-268,456-467; commits b534f47a7 (extraction), ea79ecca7 (PR20 GHA topology), 16870dbec (REB-532/ADR0026).

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [7/10] DOSSIER B — Direction arbitration & the baseline lineage: WHY + the digest risk

ORIGIN INCIDENT: commit 16870dbec (2026-06-25) / class REB-532. Before it, _diff_fields did UNCONDITIONAL local-wins -> a Jira-side field edit was reverted to local every pass (verified live: assigning a ticket in Jira reverted to unassigned). Fix = three-way merge with a common ANCESTOR: local==baseline => local unchanged => divergence is Jira-side => suppress outbound, mirror inbound; local!=baseline => local edit => local-wins. The ancestor is the ONLY direction signal (the inbound differ carries none). Absent baseline => local-wins (safe/lossy); corrupt baseline/store => fail CLOSED (an empty store treats every ticket as unbound -> mass-CREATE duplicate Jira issues, binding_store.py:126-148).

SHAPE-TOLERANCE predates the baseline (bug 85a1, code fossils outbound_fields.py:201-261): Jira returns description as ADF dict, assignee as {accountId,displayName,emailAddress}, status/priority as {name} — literal == vs local scalars fired every pass ("21-mutation idempotency churn"). Fixed by normalizing BOTH sides through one path: _extract_jira_field (ADF->adf_to_text, {name}->.name), _assignee_matches (permissive one-of-three), rstrip text. Commit e57df4539 is the NORMALIZATION-ASYMMETRY fossil: reconcile-check compared RAW Jira vs local WITHOUT the differ's normalization -> ~3660 FALSE discrepancies while the differ dispatched ~0. Lesson: normalization must be SYMMETRIC or every verdict silently corrupts.

edge->level + the CAUTIOUS ROLLOUT (epic 3006-e198; ADR 0026): baf7-868d (foundation: pure classify() + per-binding baseline on BindingStore + circuit breaker + census, wired into nothing) -> 7d23-106a (Phase-1 dual-write SHADOW behind baseline_dual_write, logs baseline_shadow_check, consumed by no one) -> a118-fa8e (Phase-3 consumer swap: re-point both _local_matches_prev sites from prev to get_baseline; 30 consecutive divergent=0 passes over ~4h/~854 bindings, then flip; first flag-ON pass 22 mutations byte-identical to pre-flip) -> d6bd-95c9 (retire flags, hardcode always-on; AC6 = decision-pin regression test with verified revert-teeth). Commits c1e494276, 1cb524c1a, b76dd09a1, c4d58a306; Gerrit 434/437/441/659.
WHY the 5 fields = _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS {title,description,priority,status,assignee}: 3-way merge only matters where BOTH sides can author = exactly the inbound-mirrored set. NUANCE: _BASELINE_FIELDS uses JIRA name "summary" but _INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS uses LOCAL "title" -> the suppression guard NEVER fires for summary/title (a documented pre-existing partial no-op pinned by a118's test; effective suppression = 4 fields).

INVARIANTS (violation reopens REB-532): (1) the ancestor VALUE must exist and be correct; (2) normalization SYMMETRIC (e57df4539); (3) absent=>None=>local-wins, corrupt-store=>abort — note an individually-wrong-but-well-formed baseline is NOT caught, just produces a wrong verdict; (4) baseline advanced only from CONFIRMED in-window bindings, stored RAW (set_baseline filters to 5 fields, no normalization); (5) direction-preservation is a first-class regression cell.

BEARING ON baseline-as-DIGEST: the baseline is read ONLY for equality (classify.direction_is_inbound local==baseline; outbound_fields _local_matches_prev/_jira_matches_prev) — nothing reconstructs/materializes/displays it -> digest NOT architecturally blocked. BUT the compare is NOT "two canonical forms byte-identical"; risks that flip a verdict (=> REB-532 returns): 
- R1 ASSIGNEE (THE KILLER): _assignee_matches is a ONE-TO-MANY set-membership test (local matches ANY of {emailAddress,accountId,displayName}); a single digest encodes ONE identity. baseline=digest(accountId) vs local stored as displayName => current says MATCH, digest says MISMATCH => local-wins reversion. Not trivially avoidable (needs a hot-path identity resolver, the exact thing _assignee_matches avoided). RECOMMENDATION: EXCLUDE assignee from digesting; keep its raw value.
- R2 ADF canonicalization instability (hash the post-adf_to_text+rstrip TEXT, never the dict); R3 rstrip parity; R4 None (no-baseline=>local-wins) vs digest("")-empty must stay distinguishable; R5 unicode NFC/NFD; R6 status/priority hash the .name; R7 no over-truncation (>=128-bit floor).
IF pursued: derive the digest from the EXACT existing normalizers (never hand-roll), extend the direction-preservation property suite FIRST with R1-R5 adversarial shape cases (existing cells use single-form fixtures and would pass while assignee regresses), then gate via dual-write shadow -> N divergent=0 -> flip -> retire (a118/d6bd template).

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [8/10] DOSSIER C — Binding lifecycle & identity: WHY (each rule = a production incident)

The binding store maps local_id<->jira_key and is the AUTHORITATIVE synced-relationship set. Lessons L9-L17 + c244, each incident-forced:
- L9 (rebar_id_audit.py:66-90, story 4496): unaudited rebar-id label writes minted ghost/duplicate identities -> ONLY 3 of 9 dispatch leaves may write a rebar-id label (outbound_create+inbound_create add, inbound_clean_label delete); every write audited. Identity is unrepairable after the fact.
- L10 (bug 4354, differ.py:457-504): a bound issue in curr-not-prev was mis-classified unbound-new -> minted a phantom jira-dig-NNNN local AND wrote a ghost rebar-id:jira-dig-5029 label back to Jira (observed 2026-05-29 DIG-5029). Fix: label-derived-binding suppression — a rebar-id-labeled snapshot key stands the snapshot differ down.
- L11 (story 7a75, invariants.py:234-307): double-bind (two Jira issues claim one local_id) -> quarantine offenders, capped per pass (can't know which claimant is legit; auto-repair risks destroying the real link).
- L13 (bug 1e08, outbound_differ.py): a bound key absent from the snapshot diffed against {} re-emitted every field every pass. Fix: membership != value; liveness resolved by a bounded, rotated direct GET (200=alive overlay, 404=deleted, else defer). Classifier returns a FOUR-way ObservedJira state (PRESENT|CONFIRMED_404|ABSENT_IN_WINDOW|TRANSPORT_ERROR), never a boolean.
- L14/L15 (bug 1e08, binding_store.py:403-448): retirement requires N CONSECUTIVE confirmed-404s (RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE default 3); a 200 resets; retirement is a REVERSIBLE soft-delete to the SEPARATE bindings-retired.json. ASYMMETRIC failure: bindings.json fails CLOSED (corrupt=>abort, else mass-duplicate); bindings-retired.json fails OPEN (corrupt=>empty+alert; a wrongly-live retired binding costs one wasted GET).
- L16 (bug 0702, outbound_differ.py:623-634): a 200 overlay is shared to inbound (avoids 2nd GET); 404/transport DELIBERATELY excluded so a gone issue is never inbound-mirrored (retirement stays outbound-owned).
- L17 (bug f6cc, fetcher.py:23-94): a single JQL hit the ~1000-issue ACLI ceiling -> Done backlog looked absent -> mass-retire. Fix: split JQL (status!=Done active + status=Done ORDER BY updated capped at _DONE_RECENT_CAP); Done-beyond-cap is alive-out-of-window, NOT deleted. Circuit breaker (refuse a pass mutating >N% of bindings) = defense-in-depth.
- c244 (binding_store.py:325-336, commit cbfb664ec): proven 404 on a still-local ticket => re-create Jira SAME pass (create_after_hard_delete); bind_confirm drops the stale reverse[old_key].
- Write-ahead protocol (binding_store.py:289-336,479-536, story 9622): bind_pending -> create -> record_pending_key -> plant marker -> bind_confirm -> save; recover_pending_bindings re-derives PENDING (never confirmed) from the rebar-id label at startup with NO Jira search.

"AUTHORITATIVE yet a derived cache" reconciled: AUTHORITATIVE operationally (the pass reads it for identity; corruption fails the pass CLOSED, _ids.py:56 "the authoritative Jira<->rebar mapping"); DERIVED by provenance (ground truth = the rebar-id label on the Jira issue [L9] + the local ticket's local_id; bindings.json is a fast, rebuildable, drift-corrected index — recover_pending_bindings, check_dual_identity_complete, bridge_fsck.audit_binding_drift). This is exactly why epic 6c9c DROPPED WS-1 (event-sourcing the data) — the convergence loop already detects+self-heals drift.
WHY ordinary clones read bindings.json (_ids.py:50-75): _resolve_via_binding_store resolves a Jira key -> local ticket dir via the `reverse` index for generic ID resolution (`rebar show REB-310`); can't be reconciler-only because the reconciler runs in CI not in dev/agent clones. Best-effort/never-raises; touches ONLY `reverse` (identity), NEVER the baseline.

BEARING: digest is IDENTITY-SAFE — grep proves `baseline` is read by ZERO of rebar_id_audit.py (L9), invariants.py (L11), differ.py (L10), _ids.py (clone reader). Drift KINDS (audit_binding_drift, census) are baseline-independent (classify.py:148 explicitly does NOT consume baseline for lifecycle routing). The digest's ONLY hazard is ADR 0026 field arbitration ([7]). One-time reclaim: recover_pending_bindings reads the LIVE in-memory store (not history); retirement is the SEPARATE bindings-retired.json — both unaffected. BUT the fail-closed corruption path restores via `git show tickets:.../bindings.json` (binding_store.py:145-146) => the reclaim MUST preserve the last-known-good bindings.json revision + keep the `.bridge_state/* merge=ours` attribute + exclude bindings-retired.json.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
### [9/10] DOSSIER D — Coordination & storage posture: WHY + the one-time reclaim flag-day

EPHEMERAL-GHA TOPOLOGY (reconcile-bridge.yml): */20 cron, ubuntu-latest, timeout 60, fetch-depth 0, concurrency group reconcile-bridge cancel-in-progress=false. The reconciler is a TEMPLATE clients copy verbatim -> must run on stock hosted infra with NO persistent box; each pass = a fresh clone discarded at job end. The only "persistent" variant is the opt-in RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS flag (self-re-dispatch; warned self-hosted-only) — still chained-ephemeral, not a daemon. Ephemerality FORCES all durable state into git+origin (why .bridge_state is committed and the lock is a pushed ref) and forces fetch-depth 0 (shallow defeats merge-base/compaction, bug f193) + merge-not-rebase commit-back.

merge=ours DERIVED-CACHE POSTURE (init.py:56-63; sync.py): .bridge_state/* committed AND merge=ours (local-wins) because (a) off-git dies with the runner and the arbitration ancestor must survive; (b) merge=union is WRONG — it line-unions JSON into INVALID JSON; (c) `ours` because .bridge_state is the LONE non-disjoint shared path (all event files are UUID-named append-only-disjoint, never collide) and is a per-pass REGENERABLE cache the next pass rebuilds. push.py names prev_snapshot.json + bindings.json "reconciler-REGENERABLE files" (bugs 12a6/6818 stash/merge/pop). Rests on the 97e7/WU-2/3 UNION reconvergence (sync.py _do_reconverge/_union_merge): non-destructive, keeps both parents, stock git gc safe; conflict => abort+keep-local+hint-fsck, NEVER reset (the pre-97e7 reset --hard orphaned un-pushed local commits — the forcing data-loss incident).

COORDINATION SPLIT (ADR 0031 / epic 6c9c dust-troth-naval): pass-lock/phase-gate moved OFF-tree to bare refs/reconciler/lock + refs/reconciler/gate (create-only CAS acquire, observed-oid CAS release, skew-proof relative-duration lease + heartbeat/fence). "A lock is not ticket data." Children 524d/7522/2711/9ed2. WS-1 (event-sourcing the binding DATA off-branch) EXPLICITLY DROPPED — quote: "WS-1 dropped because Level-triggered bridge convergence (3006 + ADRs 0026-0029 + the 8de5 classifier/canary) already made binding drift detected and self-healing and bindings.json is a derived cache." The reconciler lock guards WASTED WORK (overlapping passes), never CORRUPTION — so a lost-race/stale .bridge_state copy self-corrects next pass and stays a committed derived cache; only the coordination state (needing cross-clone consensus) moved off-branch. Task 0241 (move .bridge_state off-branch) was SUPERSEDED by this drop.

gc-CORRUPTION (bug 88eb, "ADR 0051" — NOTE: not a committed file on this checkout; adr/ tops at 0050; named in the fix work): git>=2.47 `git commit` spawns a DETACHED `git maintenance run --auto` repack OUTSIDE rebar's lock -> races concurrent writers on the shared object DB -> corruption. gc.auto=0 does NOT fix it (git>=2.47 gates on maintenance.auto). Fix: FOREGROUND maintenance (gc.autoDetach=false + maintenance.autoDetach=false, unset gc.auto). The 97e7 reachability invariant answers "gc won't delete objects I need"; it is ORTHOGONAL to "a concurrent repack corrupts the pack while I write." A one-time filter-repo reclaim is SERIAL/quiesced so not exposed to the 88eb concurrency race (with auto-maint off).

TRUST/IDENTITY (authorship.py): ancestry-based — verify_authorship_at_commit builds the trust root from keyring records live as-of the event's INTRODUCING commit; key valid iff its add-commit is an ANCESTOR (git merge-base --is-ancestor) and revoke isn't; event->commit is RELATIVE (resolve_event_commit via git log --diff-filter=A). Everything is topology/ancestry, NOT literal SHA equality -> a CONSISTENT rewrite that preserves the DAG + keeps every event/keyring file STILL VERIFIES. THE ONE SHA-BOUND PIN: enforce_since="0cf8c035..." (rebar.toml:105, require_authenticated=true :96, now a PRE-merge whole-store Verified gate). _is_enforced (verify_authorship.py:263) does merge-base --is-ancestor <since> <commit> and FAILS CLOSED TO ENFORCED on any git error. A filter-repo rewrite destroys that literal SHA -> every event fail-closes to enforced -> the grandfather boundary collapses -> the whole-store gate fails. MUST re-pin enforce_since (and verify.opcert_enforce_since if set) via the filter-repo commit-map IN THE SAME PUSH.

ONE-TIME RECLAIM FLAG-DAY (8 steps): 1) disable */20 + RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS, drain in-flight pass, break-glass refs/reconciler/lock+gate. 2) FREEZE all writers. 3) filter-repo strip old .bridge_state blobs (NEVER touch event <hex>/<ts>-<uuid>-<TYPE>.json or keyring files), capture commit-map. 4) re-pin enforce_since (+opcert) to mapped SHA in the same push. 5) force-push rewritten tickets to origin. 6) re-clone/reset EVERY persistent auto-pushing clone to rewritten origin/tickets BEFORE it next writes — else sync.py:90-92 --allow-unrelated-histories UNION drags the stripped blobs back. VECTORS on this host: the operator-box main-checkout .tickets-tracker; every feature-worktree .tickets-tracker under .claude/worktrees/*; any running rebar-mcp process (restart it). NOTE the hourly origin/main tracker (CLAUDE.local.md) installs the TOOL BINARY from the code mirror — it does NOT clone/push tickets, so it is NOT a drag-back vector (correcting an earlier framing); the thing to quiesce is the running MCP/tool PROCESS. The GHA runner re-clones fresh so is safe IF the reconciler stays PAUSED until origin is rewritten. 7) re-init each tracker (applies foreground-maintenance gc config; git>=2.47 ignores gc.auto). 8) run `rebar verify-identity --all` -> 0 enforced-not-verified against the new pin; then resume the reconciler.

BEARING: (a) content-narrowing and (b) the debug artifact PRESERVE the storage posture (still regenerable caches, single JSON blobs, merge=ours still right); narrowing actually strengthens it by shrinking the only non-disjoint churning path. (c) is safe on the trust-ANCESTRY axis but has two hard coordination failure modes: the enforce_since re-pin (else the pre-merge gate bricks the store) and the --allow-unrelated-histories drag-back (else any un-converged clone resurrects the blobs).

comments.body:
### [10/10] CONVERSATION DECISIONS + RECOMMENDED PLAN + OPEN GATES + RESEARCH

USER STEERS (settled, do not re-litigate): (1) the .bridge_state files MUST stay committed in the repo — critical so the reconciler runs consistently across ephemeral CI jobs AND local environments (this killed the "make prev local-only/gitignored" option). (2) history is USEFUL for debugging but the volume is EXCESSIVE — bound it, don't eliminate. (3) user was SKEPTICAL of "prev is redundant" -> forced the adversarial proof that found prev is load-bearing (see [3]). (4) .bridge_state stays a committed on-branch merge=ours derived cache (settled by epic 6c9c; WS-1 dropped) — a separate ref revives a dropped decision.

DECISIONS MADE (via explicit choice):
- DEBUG TRAIL: keep a SEPARATE bounded full-Jira-snapshot debug artifact, MAX 1 snapshot/day, 15-DAY retention (<=15 snapshots). Decoupled from the tiny functional key-set prev.
- EXISTING ~337 MB: ONE-TIME coordinated reclaim (reconciler-paused, all-clones-converged filter-repo + lockstep enforce_since re-pin) — see [9] flag-day.
- bindings.json: INVESTIGATE NOW (done, [5]) and fold into the design.

RECOMMENDED PLAN (TABLED — implement later, in this order):
1. prev_snapshot -> KEY-SET (dict {jira_key:{}}), AFTER clearing the _emit_both open gate ([4]). Near-eliminates the 155 MB grower. Dead-code cleanup alongside: remove outbound_differ prev plumbing (OutboundDiffConfig.prev_snapshot :364, :526, :795 threading, outbound_fields.py:416 fallback) + dead seed_baselines_from_snapshot.
2. bindings.json CHURN GUARD (drop/guard baseline_advanced_at + write-when-changed in set_baseline) — biggest+safest, collapses the ~987-version-per-pass trajectory to real-change-only. THEN TEXT NORMALIZE (adf_to_text desc + status/priority .name, -66%, no migration). DIGEST is OPTIONAL and only behind a dual-write-shadow rollout; if pursued, EXCLUDE assignee (R1 killer, [7]).
3. DEBUG ARTIFACT: dated disjoint path (e.g. debug/<date>-<uuid>.json so it never collides — no merge driver needed), written <=1/day, pruned to 15 days by NOT-writing rather than history rewrite, kept OUT of fail-closed logic and ideally out of the .bridge_state commit-back or clearly scoped.
4. ONE-TIME RECLAIM: the [9] 8-step quiesced flag-day. Do LAST, after go-forward growth is fixed.

OPEN GATES (must resolve BEFORE implementing):
- G1 (blocks prev key-set): resolve the _emit_both fence ([4]) via a corpus mutation-diff (prev-full vs prev-keyset) — prove branch-3 outbound updates are dropped/superseded, or skip the both-path for empty prev, or stop feeding prev to compute_mutations. Also confirm branch-2 neutering aligns with ADR 0028.
- G2 (blocks digest, if pursued): normalization parity R1-R7 ([7]); extend the direction-preservation property suite with adversarial shape cases FIRST; assignee likely excluded.
- G3 (coordination): any prev/bindings change touches the differ/field contract shared with the ACTIVE session epic 58b0 (sync correctness) — coordinate. And each reconciler-core change should ride the proven rollout template (dual-write shadow -> N divergent=0 passes -> flag flip -> retire), the a118/d6bd playbook.
- G4 (reclaim): enforce_since lockstep re-pin + converge ALL auto-pushing clones ([9]) or the rewrite is undone by --allow-unrelated-histories.

RESEARCH / PRIOR-ART (full cited report in b96a): high-commit-volume git projects converge on moving hot/high-churn derived data OFF shared history onto HTTP/CDN (crates.io sparse index RFC 2789 + periodic squash; Homebrew 4.0 JSON-over-CDN, shallow BANNED; CocoaPods/Go-modules). git-annex `git-annex` branch + `git annex forget` = the closest analog (separate union-merged metadata branch, prune history, survives uncoordinated squash via content-convergence) — its documented failure is exactly rebar's --allow-unrelated-histories drag-back ("needs a supporting version on ALL clones"). Consumer-side (shallow/partial/commit-graph) cuts CLIENT cost only, never the authoritative store; treeless partial clone RAISES server pack CPU ~4x. VERDICT for rebar: it's a distributed union-merge store, so the on-lane fix is NOT re-homing (dropped) but SHRINKING the on-branch cache content + one-time reclaim — which is this plan.

SUBAGENT INVESTIGATIONS THIS SESSION (all cited above): repo-size measurement; prev-not-redundant red/blue team; prev consumer/field-drift sizing; clone-topology; strategy pressure-test; bindings.json sizing; + 4 history dossiers A/B/C/D. Raw reports are in the session transcript; distilled with citations in entries [2]-[9].
